'''David Matravers''' (26 September 1937 – 31 May 2022) was a British mathematician and [[cosmologist]] and Professor of [[Mathematics]] at the [[University of Portsmouth]]. His research interests were in Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Cosmology.

He founded the [[Institute of Cosmology and Gravitation, University of Portsmouth|Institute of Cosmology and Gravitation]] at the University of Portsmouth.<ref name="80threport">{{cite web| url=https://www.icg.port.ac.uk/2017/12/celebrating-prof-david-matravers-at-80/| title=Celebrating Prof. David Matravers at 80| date=8 June 2022| access-date=3 June 2022| archive-date=18 September 2024| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240918115706/https://www.icg.port.ac.uk/2017/12/celebrating-prof-david-matravers-at-80/| url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://telescoper.wordpress.com/2022/06/03/r-i-p-david-matravers/ | title=R.I.P. David Matravers | date=3 June 2022 }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Following BSc and MSc studies at [[University of Natal|Natal]] and [[University of South Africa|UNISA]], he did his PhD at [[Rhodes University]] in South Africa under the supervision of [[Hanno Rund]] in 1972.

In 1990 David Matravers joined the [[University of Portsmouth]] as Head of School of Mathematical Studies, and became Head of School of Computer Science and Mathematics in 1997. At Portsmouth he founded a research group in General Relativity and Cosmology,<ref name="80threport" /> that in 2002 became the [[Institute of Cosmology and Gravitation, University of Portsmouth|Institute of Cosmology and Gravitation]].

==Publications==
David Matravers published more than 50 research papers in [[General relativity|General Relativity]] and [[cosmology]]. 

In 2019 he published the book "How Cosmologists Explain the Universe to Friends and Family", with Karim A. Malik, ISBN 978-3-030-32733-0.
